tools_used: courtlistener MCP (search, dockets, docket-entries, read_document, get_endpoint_schema, get_more_results)
helpful: Provisioned petition text (it named the lead case and the hold request)
Statpack per-Term band table for the pooled anchor
read_document for the Fifth Circuit opinion under review
open-events as a cheap check that the lead case is still open
Public supremecourt.gov docket page for the lead case
gaps: No way to look a corpus case up by docket number or caption: query is a structured filter with a 500-row cap, so the lead case's corpus row (distribution count, response dates, amicus count) was unreachable
CourtListener's search index does not cover these SCOTUS dockets and its docket-entries endpoint is empty for them, so finding a companion docket took a date-window listing plus docket-number probes
WebFetch of this case's own supremecourt.gov page returned empty content twice
The statpack has no cut for petitions on which a response was requested, the strongest signal on this docket
notes: A companion/hold petition is nearly a deterministic function of its lead case; a provisioned pointer to the lead docket's snapshot (or a corpus lookup by docket number) would replace about fifteen retrieval calls.
